summary:
Workplace Insight announces Issue 21 of Works magazine, now available as a free digital edition, covering workplace design, people, places and technology. The issue frames itself as arriving at a moment of rapid technological change, proliferating AI-generated content and continuing post-pandemic repercussions, which it argues favour publications and workplaces that emphasise the human, physical and connected.

Major case studies include: Studio McW's new East London headquarters at Printing House Yard, where the architectural practice applied lessons from residential design to its own office, focusing on light, materials, comfort, routine and psychological ease rather than simply making an office resemble a home; Reply House in Turin, created by ACPV ARCHITECTS for technology consultancy Reply inside the historic former De Sonnaz Barracks, exploring adaptive reuse and how existing buildings can be adapted for contemporary work without erasing their retained qualities; and DLA Piper's new Leeds workplace at City Square House, which consolidates teams previously split across two locations into a single office offering collaborative space, hospitality, wellbeing facilities and varied settings for hybrid working.

An interview features Giesela Bailey, Managing Director of Flokk UK and Ireland, who discusses her path from aspiring farmer through food and fashion to furniture, calls for more manufacturer collaboration and talent from outside the sector, describes salespeople shifting from product specialists to trusted advisers, and argues sustainability is now an expectation rather than a differentiator.

Other content: a Showroom product section covering adaptability, comfort, circularity and acoustics; a preview of ORGATEC returning to Cologne in October, including the 2026 Wherever Whenever Work Culture Festival with themes of Empowered Experience, Connected Cultures and Radical Impact; coverage of the new Sustainability Works magazine edited by Joanna Knight of the Sustainable Design Collective, featuring Digital Product Passports and a reuse-first case study of Grant Thornton UK's London HQ; Viewfinder projects from Nigeria and China; a Stephanie Fitzgerald comment on Gen Z unease about AI; and an Out of Office piece on AI consciousness.

claims.claim: Sustainability has become an expectation in the furniture industry rather than a differentiating sales claim
claims.attribution: Giesela Bailey, Managing Director, Flokk UK & Ireland
